info.GpuCoreOffsetMhz:
Shifts the GPU clock curve by a common offset. Positive adds clock at the same voltage anchors; negative reduces clock.

Too much offset can cause artifacts or driver crashes. Tune in small steps and check under load. If the preset also contains a custom V/F curve, the curve wins and the global clock offset is skipped. If a custom curve is currently active, Apply first sets its deviations to 0; Restore brings the curve back.
info.GpuMemoryOffsetMhz:
Raises or lowers the VRAM clock. More memory bandwidth can help when the GPU is memory-limited.

An excessive offset can cause artifacts, instability or lower performance. After each change, check that the tuning actually improves performance and remains stable.
info.GpuVfCurve:
Edits the target clock at the GPU's existing voltage anchors. A common use is undervolting: tune a suitable clock at a lower voltage anchor.

The anchors stay fixed; the curve does not enforce a hard voltage ceiling. Boost and stability still depend on the GPU, load and driver. Replaces the global GPU clock offset. New presets and Reset start from the driver's factory curve, not from a curve that is currently applied.
info.MaxFan:
Requests the HP BIOS Max-Fan override for both fans. This adds cooling headroom under load, at noticeably higher noise.

Off only releases this override. It does not confirm a safe handover to BIOS automatic control.
info.GpuCustomTgp:
Ticked = on, unticked = off; the preset always writes the state. Turns the HP BIOS cTGP offset on or off. On by default; only the dashboard mode Quiet turns it off.

According to the BIOS table, cTGP gives the GPU +20 W, but only in the Unleashed and Performance modes, so here together with Dynamic Boost. In Balanced, cTGP has no effect (measured on 30 October 2026). Readback and restore as for the other fields.
info.GpuDynamicBoostLimitMw:
Sets the GPU ceiling for Dynamic Boost (stock 115 W, verified up to 135 W on HP 8E35 / RTX 5070 Laptop). Uses a fully reversible driver-registry VBIOS override with no EEPROM flash, no Secure Boot change and no Windows Defender exclusion.

Changing to a different wattage briefly restarts the NVIDIA driver (screens flash briefly). The app then reads back the active limit via NVML. Restoring the preset or applying a stock mode returns to stock 115 W. The maximum slider ceiling can be raised in Settings.
info.HpSharedPowerMw:
Shared CPU and GPU power budget that Dynamic Boost distributes. Factory value 45 W, HP Unleashed sets 72 W; the firmware also accepts higher values (tested up to 115 W).

The firmware cannot report this value back: it is written before the preset but not confirmed, and Restore does not reset it. Every HP performance mode writes it again.

Like the OMEN Hub, the slider covers 55–72 W. Older values outside stay until you move the slider.
hp.err.tpp_range: TPP must be whole watts between 1 and 254 W.
info.GpuPowerLimitMw:
Sets the NVIDIA driver's offered power limit in watts. Bounds and the configured original must be readable so the app can verify and restore the change.

That original query is unavailable on the reference laptop, so this control remains unavailable there. A reported limit is not measured power draw.
info.GpuUnleashed:
Ticked = on, unticked = off (default); the preset always writes the state. On: when applying, the app switches internally to the Unleashed mode (GPU up to about 112 W, measured under load) and turns NVIDIA Dynamic Boost on; all other values of the preset still apply. TPP follows the preset, without a TPP field 72 W as in Unleashed; CPU values the preset leaves out follow Unleashed. On battery, where Unleashed does not exist, Performance is set. The fans follow the mode.

Off: the app sets the Balanced mode with Dynamic Boost off; the GPU limit is then 80 W.

The mode has no readback and is not undone by Restore. With "Keep preset" it is written again when the GPU limit under load falls to 80 W or less.
info.CpuTemperatureLimitC:
Target temperature for CPU control. A saved value becomes a confirmed setting only after successful application and readback.

CPU temperature (Tctl) on the dashboard is a separate measurement. A rejected or merely saved preset does not change a temperature limit. A later independent readback is needed to check whether the limit persists.
info.CpuStapmLimitMw: Legacy STAPM instruction. Independent STAPM control is not enabled in this app; use the supported Slow/PPT limits instead.
info.CpuSlowPptLimitMw:
Sets the CPU's Slow power limit through the app's SMU path. Together with PPT, current and temperature limits, it constrains sustained load.

A lower value can keep sustained loads cooler. More watts add boost headroom only when another limit is not already binding. The app's value takes precedence and also overwrites values set by other programs such as the HP service.

With Dynamic Boost (Unleashed) the slider covers 15–80 W in 1-W steps (45–80 W also written as firmware PL1; below 45 W the app reversibly disables NVPCF's 80 W CPU overwriter and writes Slow directly via SMU). Without Dynamic Boost it spans 15–160 W.
info.CpuPptLimitMw:
Sets the CPU's Package Power Tracking (PPT) limit. It works together with Slow, TDC/EDC and the temperature limit.

More watts can add boost headroom; fewer watts reduce the power budget. Actual performance depends on load, cooling and other limits. The app's value takes precedence and also overwrites values set by other programs such as the HP service.

In Unleashed mode (Dynamic Boost), Apply reversibly disables NVPCF's CPU TDP overwriter (sub-function #9) so your Fast and Slow limits hold steady while Dynamic Boost stays fully active. Restore returns NVPCF to factory defaults.
info.CpuTdcMa:
Sets the sustained CPU current limit, TDC, in amperes. It constrains boost alongside power and temperature limits.

Less current can reduce VRM load. A higher limit does not guarantee a higher clock; the offered bounds do not certify stable sustained operation.
info.CpuEdcMa:
Sets the CPU's EDC current limit for short load spikes, in amperes. A tight limit can constrain boost.

A higher value alone does not guarantee extra performance. Power limits, cooling and stability still matter.
info.CpuPboScalar:
Sets the PBO scalar, which affects how boost uses its voltage and time margins.

Higher values can increase power and heat without a measurable performance gain. 1× was tested on the reference device; the entire offered range is not qualified as stable operation.
info.CpuBoostProfile: Legacy boost profile. This separate AMD control path is not implemented. Windows processor boost and EPP provide the supported boost-tuning policies.
info.CpuCurveOptimizerAllCore:
Adjusts the CPU voltage/frequency curve for all cores together. Values are Curve Optimizer steps, not fixed millivolts.

Negative values can improve efficiency and boost. Overly aggressive values may become unstable even at idle or light load. Check small changes under load and in everyday use.
info.CpuCurveOptimizerPerCore:
Tunes Curve Optimizer for each core separately. Undervolting headroom varies between cores; the fastest core does not automatically have the most margin.

Values are steps, not fixed mV. If the preset contains both, per-core wins and all-core is skipped.
info.CpuAllCoreVoltageOffsetMv: Direct all-core voltage offset in mV. This control path is not enabled. Curve Optimizer uses its own steps and is not a fixed mV offset.
info.AmdCpuVoltageMv: Fixed CPU voltage for manual OC. This control path is not enabled in the current app.
info.AmdCpuClockMhz: Fixed CPU clock for manual OC. This control path is not enabled in the current app.
info.WindowsBoostMode:
Chooses the Windows power plan's processor boost policy.

Disabled does not request boost above base clock. Enabled and Aggressive allow more boost; the efficient variants put more weight on energy use. Actual CPU behavior also depends on the driver, firmware and other limits.
info.WindowsMinimumProcessorPercent:
Sets the Windows plan's minimum processor state in percent. This is a performance policy, not a measured clock.

A higher value can affect responsiveness and idle power. The actual effect depends on the system.
info.WindowsMaximumProcessorPercent:
Sets the Windows plan's maximum processor state in percent. This is a policy, not a fixed clock target.

Values below 100% can constrain performance and, depending on the system, boost. Use Processor boost when you specifically want to disable boost.
info.WindowsProcessorEppPercent:
Energy Performance Preference balances performance and efficiency.

0% favors performance; 100% favors efficiency. It does not set a fixed clock or power draw. Useful when tuning a balanced or battery preset.
info.WindowsCoreParkingMinPercent:
Sets the Windows policy's minimum share of unparked cores. Higher values allow less core parking and can increase idle power.

This is not a live count of active cores; Windows and CPU firmware determine actual behavior.
info.WindowsCoreParkingMaxPercent:
Sets the Windows policy's maximum share of unparked cores. A lower value can constrain available multicore performance.

This is a policy, not a measurement of active cores.
info.CpuCcdAffinity:
Selects CCDs for the foreground program: 1 = first CCD, 2 = second CCD, 3 = both. The app's helper applies process affinity and retains the original assignment.

A single CCD can change a game's behavior but reduces the available cores. Protected programs, such as those with anti-cheat, may reject the change.
info.WindowsEnergyMode:
Chooses the Windows power mode between efficiency, balanced and performance.

Windows applies the power mode only on the Balanced power plan. Without a plan in the preset, Apply switches to Balanced; if the preset selects another plan, that plan wins and the power mode is skipped.
info.WindowsPowerPlan:
Changes the active Windows power plan. The app preserves the original selection and, where relevant, the target plan's CPU policies.

A plan name alone does not guarantee a particular clock or power draw.
info.DisplayRefreshRateHz:
Chooses an offered refresh rate for the primary Windows display. Higher Hz can make motion smoother; lower Hz can reduce power use.

Only currently available display modes are used.
info.GraphicsMode:
Stores the BIOS boot preference for graphics mode (MUX). Hybrid, discrete GPU and, where offered, integrated GPU are separate preferences.

The change needs a restart. Reading back the BIOS value does not confirm actual display routing or a powered-off NVIDIA GPU. Physical switching and iGPU-only battery operation still need validation.

info.mode:
Chooses a fixed laptop performance-mode preset. The app sends the examined BIOS commands directly.

Quiet: quietest Balanced step, 55 W sustained CPU limit (108 A TDC / 160 A EDC), Dynamic Boost off on AC.
Balanced (Standard): 55 W sustained CPU limit (108 A TDC / 160 A EDC), Dynamic Boost on.
Performance: 60 W sustained CPU limit (108 A TDC / 160 A EDC), cTGP and Dynamic Boost on.
Unleashed: AC required, 80 W sustained CPU limit (108 A TDC / 160 A EDC) and the model-specific shared-budget request.

The full current BIOS mode is not readable. GPU flags and available CPU values are checked. A failed switch attempts Balanced; this is not a restore of an unknown original mode.

curve.help:
GPU curve
Drag: move a point or the selected range vertically.
Shift + drag point: move the loaded base curve/selection.
Alt + drag point: move the current draft/selection evenly.
Ctrl + drag point: tilt the curve around the opposite end point.
Shift + drag in empty chart: select a voltage range.
Shift + Left/Right: extend the selection. Ctrl + A: all points.
Shift + Enter: flatten the selection; without one, plateau from the point.
Esc or double-click: clear the selection; Esc while dragging: cancel.

Common controls
Left/Right: choose a point. Up/Down: 1 MHz or 1 %.
Ctrl + Up/Down: 10 steps. Enter: edit the number field.
Ctrl + Z: undo. Ctrl + Y / Ctrl + Shift + Z: redo.
Ctrl + D: reset to the loaded draft. Ctrl + S: save profile.
Mouse wheel or +/−: zoom voltage/temperature. Ctrl: Y axis.
Shift + mouse wheel: scroll horizontally. Ctrl + 0: whole curve.

Fans
Ctrl + Left/Right: edit temperature. Shift: larger steps.
Right-click: add or delete a point. Ins: add point. Del: remove point.
One shared curve applies to CPU and GPU fans; saving hands it to the fan service.

The GPU curve is applied through a preset.
Fixed voltage/clock lock and OC Scanner are not available yet.

info.hold_preset:
Keeps the values of the last applied preset against other programs (such as the HP service) and against the firmware (HP BIOS, NVIDIA Dynamic Boost), which reset CPU limits and GPU flags. When ticked, the app checks every 5 seconds and rewrites only values that differ: PPT, Slow, TDC, EDC, temperature limit, PBO, Curve Optimizer, cTGP and Dynamic Boost, with Dynamic Boost also the Unleashed mode.

Not during Apply or Restore and not after a dashboard mode. If a value is overwritten again right after three rewrites in a row, the app pauses for about 5 minutes and then tries again. Every correction is listed in preset-hold.log in the data folder.
settings.admin_required: Omen Hub++ needs administrator rights for this. Restart the app and confirm the Windows prompt.
info.autostart: Starts Omen Hub++ when you sign in to Windows through a Task Scheduler task with administrator rights (no prompt), with its window or, with “Start in the tray”, only in the tray. No preset is applied; use “Apply at sign-in” in the preset editor for that.
info.close_to_tray: Closing and minimizing only hide the window. Omen Hub++ keeps running in the tray, so the battery preset and status stay active. When off, closing exits the app.
info.hp_service:
Stops the HP service HPOmenCap (OmenCap.exe) and sets its start type to Disabled. While it runs it overwrites CPU power limits, and presets with CPU PPT or Slow limits are refused.

Afterwards the BIOS and Omen Hub++ control the hardware alone. The previous start type is saved; turning this off restores it and starts the service. A Windows Update of the HP component can enable the service again.

The switch takes effect at once, without Save.
info.battery:
When the charger is unplugged, Omen Hub++ applies this preset or mode automatically. When it is plugged in again, it returns to the preset last applied on AC (Balanced if none is known).

A preset applied by hand while on battery stays after plugging in. “Off” turns automatic switching off. Omen Hub++ must be running for this, in the tray is enough.

Taken over with “Save”.
info.battery_behaviour:
When the charger is unplugged while this preset is active, Omen Hub++ applies the preset chosen here automatically. When the charger returns, the app goes back to this preset. “Off” leaves everything unchanged on battery.

A preset applied by hand on battery stays until the charger is connected again. Omen Hub++ must be running, the tray is enough. The choice is kept with “Save”.

curve.help_gpu:
Mouse
Hover a point: voltage, clock and offset from the NVIDIA default.
Drag a point: change its clock; a point inside the selection moves the whole selection.
Shift + drag a point: move the curve or selection using the shape of the NVIDIA default curve.
Alt + drag a point: move the curve or selection keeping its current shape.
Ctrl + drag a point: tilt the curve around the opposite edge point.
Shift + drag on free space: select a voltage range.
Click on free space or double-click: clear the selection.
Wheel: zoom the voltage axis. Ctrl + wheel: clock axis. Shift + wheel: pan.

Keyboard
Left/Right, Home/End: select a point. With Shift: extend the selection.
Ctrl + A: select all points. Esc: clear the selection, cancel a drag.
Up/Down: ±1 MHz, with Ctrl ±10 MHz.
Shift or Alt + Up/Down: move the curve or selection as when dragging.
Enter: edit the MHz field. Enter in the field sets the point or the whole selection.
Shift + Enter: flatten the selection to the selected point's clock; without a selection, plateau from the point.
Ctrl + Z: undo. Ctrl + Y or Ctrl + Shift + Z: redo.
Ctrl + D: restore the curve from opening. Ctrl + R: reset to the NVIDIA default.
+/−: zoom, with Ctrl the clock axis. Ctrl + 0: whole curve. Ctrl + S: use curve.
F1 or i: this help.

Use curve changes only the preset draft. Save it and apply it explicitly.
curve.help_fan:
Mouse
Hover a point: temperature and fan value.
Drag a point: change temperature and value.
Click on free space: add a point.
Double-click a point: remove it.
Wheel: zoom the temperature axis. Ctrl + wheel: value axis. Shift + wheel: pan.

Keyboard
Left/Right, Home/End: select a point.
Up/Down: ±1 %, with Ctrl or Shift ±10 %.
Ctrl + Left/Right: temperature ±1 °C, with Shift ±10 °C.
Insert: add a point. Delete: remove the point.
Enter: edit the value field. Enter in the field sets the point.
Ctrl + Z: undo. Ctrl + Y or Ctrl + Shift + Z: redo.
Ctrl + D or Ctrl + R: restore the curve from opening.
+/−: zoom, with Ctrl the value axis. Ctrl + 0: whole curve. Ctrl + S: use curve.
F1 or i: this help.
